title: Build a Responsive Community Tech Festival Website
summary: Apply the CSS skills learned on the cumulative portfolio to a fresh responsive community tech festival website.

sketchBlocks.title: Project scenario and learner role
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
**Scenario:** Jordan Lee is preparing the same portfolio site for recruiter and client review. The content is already written and the semantic HTML is already correct, but the project gallery needs to adapt cleanly from narrow screens to wider layouts.

**Your role:** You are the junior front-end developer responsible for the CSS layout pass. Do not rebuild the HTML. Improve only the presentation layer.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Work in the existing six-file portfolio
sketchBlocks.title: Work in the existing six-file portfolio
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
**Concrete workspace:** keep these inherited files exactly in place:

- `index.html`
- `about.html`
- `contact.html`
- `projects/portfolio.html`
- `styles.css`
- `images/profile.png`

Edit `styles.css` only. The HTML pages and `images/profile.png` remain unchanged. The responsive gallery work must carry every earlier cascade, box-model, and Flexbox rule forward.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Deliver a useful responsive gallery checkpoint
sketchBlocks.title: Deliver a useful responsive gallery checkpoint
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
**Deliverable:** one cumulative `styles.css` that turns the inherited portfolio content into a responsive project gallery using Grid, fluid tracks, relative sizing, and mobile-first media queries.

The finished checkpoint should keep the gallery usable on narrow screens, allow repeated content to flow into fluid columns as space grows, and add a deliberate wide-layout feature without changing the source HTML.

**Acceptance check:** preview the existing `projects/portfolio.html` at narrow and wide widths and verify that the same semantic content remains readable while the Grid adapts.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 1: Establish the festival's visual foundation
quizDraft.hint: Start with the `:root` block. Define all nine custom properties first, then use them with `var(--name)` in the page rules.

help.concept: CSS custom properties let you name a design value once and reuse it throughout the stylesheet.
help.hint_1: The first selector should be `:root`. Add the nine provided `--name: value;` declarations there.
help.hint_2: For the centered layout, group `main`, `.site-header`, and `footer`, then use `width: min(70rem, calc(100% - 2rem))` and `margin-inline: auto`.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 3: Create flexible content systems with Grid
quizDraft.prompt:
## Step 3 — Create responsive card grids

The festival has three repeated-content areas: event cards, schedule cards, and speaker cards.

### Build one shared Grid rule

Group `.event-grid`, `.schedule-grid`, and `.speaker-grid`, then add:

```css
.event-grid,
.schedule-grid,
.speaker-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(15rem, 1fr));
  gap: var(--space);
}
```

`auto-fit` creates as many columns as can fit.

`minmax(15rem, 1fr)` prevents a column from becoming narrower than `15rem` while still allowing available columns to share the remaining space.

### What you should see

A narrow preview should show fewer columns. As the preview gets wider, more cards should move onto the same row automatically.
quizDraft.hint: Use one grouped rule for all three containers. The exact track value is `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(15rem, 1fr))`.

help.concept: CSS Grid can create responsive columns automatically. `auto-fit` and `minmax()` let the available width decide how many columns fit.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 6: Finish interaction states and keyboard accessibility
quizDraft.prompt:
## Step 6 — Finish hover and keyboard focus states

The layout is complete. Now make interactive states visible for both mouse and keyboard users.

### 1. Add hover feedback

```css
nav a:hover,
.button-link:hover,
button:hover {
  color: #ffffff;
  background: var(--accent-strong);
}
```

### 2. Add keyboard focus feedback

```css
a:focus-visible,
button:focus-visible,
input:focus-visible,
select:focus-visible,
textarea:focus-visible {
  outline: 0.2rem solid #f59e0b;
  outline-offset: 0.2rem;
}
```

### Test it

Open the **Register** page and press the `Tab` key repeatedly.

Do not remove the browser focus state without replacing it.

### What you should see

Keyboard focus should produce a clear orange outline around every interactive control. Hovering navigation links or primary buttons should change them to the stronger blue.
quizDraft.hint: There are two selector groups: one for `:hover` and one for `:focus-visible`. The focus group must include links, buttons, inputs, selects, and textareas.

help.concept: Hover feedback helps pointer users, while `:focus-visible` tells keyboard users which control will receive their next action.
help.hint_1: The hover group uses `var(--accent-strong)` and keeps the text white.
help.hint_2: Use `outline: 0.2rem solid #f59e0b` and `outline-offset: 0.2rem` for the focus-visible group.
